negative_findings.result_summary: Zero usable Serbian-language sources for IFI reporting on Kosovo were found in this run. IFIs publish on Kosovo in English only; Serbian-language secondary coverage appears to originate from Serbia-based outlets that were not surfaced by this query.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The run requires sr coverage. If no sr-language IFI channel exists, sr coverage for this cell must come from Serbian-language media in Kosovo/Serbia, which needs a separate targeted query set (Latin-script Serbian, e.g. 'MMF izveštaj Kosovo bankarski sektor').

brief: For Kosovo, the IFI layer is unusually rich and English-first, and it functions as the de facto forward calendar of banking regulation: the IMF is the dominant actor through Article IV consultations, the 2019 Financial Sector Stability Review and its 2025/2026 follow-up, plus the recently closed SBA/RSF whose structural benchmarks explicitly dated items such as the SREP adoption roadmap. The World Bank contributes the payments and market-infrastructure side — most importantly the live Financial Sector Development Project (P507881, EUR ~50m) covering a development bank, credit guarantees and a fast payment system — reinforced by FinSAC in Vienna on supervision, resolution and deposit insurance. EBRD, EIB and the CEB add a second, thinner conditionality channel through country strategies, annual Transition Report country assessments and intermediated bank facilities, with EBRD's Kosovo Country Strategy 2022-2027 and Financial Sector Strategy 2026-2030 signalling policy-dialogue direction. The principal collection risks are technical rather than substantive: imf.org returns 403 to plain fetchers and the World Bank projects list is a JavaScript SPA, while local-language coverage of this cell exists only as second-hand CBK and Albanian-press reporting, with Serbian-language coverage still unproven.
